description.en: The aim of the experiment is to study and measure the Voltage, Current, Power and Power Factor in a parallel RLC circuit.
The Instructions provide step-by-step guidance on how to perform the simulation.
The AI guide will assist you in performing the simulation accurately at each step.

The CHECK button verifies all the connections to ensure that they are correct.

**Note:** If a wire is connected incorrectly, click the corresponding label number to remove the connection.
The AUTO CONNECT button makes all the connections automatically.
The ADD button adds the readings to the observation table.
The RESET button refreshes the simulation to its initial state for a fresh start.
The PRINT button allows you to print the simulation.

The Correct Values button shows a reference table containing the correct values for different R-L-C combinations, including supply voltage, current, frequency and circuit nature. Use these values to verify your calculated results.

The MCB acts as the main power switch for the experiment. It also protects the circuit by automatically disconnecting the power supply in case of an overload or short circuit. When turned ON, it supplies electrical power to the circuit.

**Rating**: 6 A, SP, 240 V AC 

**Input supply** 230 V AC, 50 Hz.

steps.narration: The MCB acts as the main power switch for the experiment. It protects the circuit by disconnecting the power supply in case of an overload or short circuit. Rating: 6 ampere, single pole, 240 volt AC. Input supply: 230 volt AC, 50 hertz.

description.en:
The autotransformer is used to obtain a variable AC output voltage from the 230 V input supply. It allows the output voltage to be varied gradually and set to 30 V for safe operation of the circuit. 

**Ratings:** 

**Max. kVA:** 4.05, Max. Load: 15 A 

** Input Voltage: **240 V, 50Hz 

**Output Voltage:** 0 - 240V AC

The resistor acts as the resistive element of the parallel RLC circuit and consumes active power. It is used to study the effect of resistance on circuit current, power, and power factor.

 **Rating:** 1 kΩ, 2 kΩ, 3 kΩ

The inductor provides the inductive branch in the parallel RLC circuit and stores energy in its magnetic field. It introduces inductive reactance, affects the circuit current and phase relationship, and contributes to the overall power factor of the circuit.

**Rating:** 2 H and 5 H

The capacitor acts as the capacitive element of the parallel RLC circuit and stores energy in its electric field. It is used to study the effect of capacitance on circuit current, phase angle, and power factor.

**Rating**: 2.2 µF and 4.7 µF

The voltmeter (V) is used to measure the voltage applied to the parallel RLC circuit. It shows the output voltage received from the autotransformer, which is adjusted to 30 V for the experiment.

**Rating**: 0–50 V

The ammeter 1 is used to measure the total current drawn by the parallel RLC circuit. It displays the current flowing from the supply due to the combined effect of the resistive, inductive, and capacitive branch currents.

**Rating**: 0–50 mA

The wattmeter is used to measure the active power consumed by the parallel RLC circuit. The measured power (P) helps in analyzing the power consumed by the resistor and studying its effect on the overall circuit behaviour.

**Rating**: 0–1 W

steps.narration: The wattmeter is used to measure the active power consumed by the parallel RLC circuit. The measured power (P) helps in analyzing the power consumed by the resistor and studying its effect on the overall circuit behaviour and power factor.

description.en:
The ammeter 2 is used to measure the current flowing through the resistor branch of the parallel RLC circuit.  

**Rating**: 0–50 mA

The ammeter 3 is used to measure the current flowing through the inductor branch of the parallel RLC circuit.

**Rating**: 0–50 mA

The ammeter 4 is used to measure the current flowing through the capacitor branch of the parallel RLC circuit.

**Rating**: 0–50 mA

This table records the selected RLC values along with the measured readings of voltage, supply current, resistive current (I_R), inductive current (I_L), capacitive current (I_C) and power during the experiment. These observations will be used to calculate the percentage error and analyse the behaviour of the parallel RLC circuit.

steps.narration: This table records the selected RLC values along with the measured readings of voltage, supply current, resistive current I R, inductive current I L, capacitive current I C, and power during the experiment. These observations are used for the error analysis and to analyse the behaviour of the parallel RLC circuit.

description.en: This panel contains the equations required to verify the readings of the Parallel RLC circuit. Use these expressions to calculate the required values and verify the results by clicking the Verify button.

This section will be used to calculate the theoretical values for the selected RLC parameters using the provided equations. After verification, the percentage error will be calculated using the specified error formula and displayed in the Error Section.

The Report button generates a summarised report of the simulation. After completing the observation table and theoretical calculations, generate the report. The report will include the time taken to complete the simulation, simulation summary, the apparatus used, recorded readings, user-calculated results and conclusion.

 **Note:** Please ensure that at least two readings are verified before generating the report.
